evidence: Tac. Dial. 28.4: cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum
Quint. 1.3.1: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est
terms.comment: The one taken before the others (prae and capiō, Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: phrase, with an infinitive or an accusative and infinitive
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.17.4: id quod caput est
Cic. de Or. 1.132: caput esse artis decēre (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 105: id caput est, that’s the main point
Traupman 106: the point is that …, quod caput est
terms.comment: The main dish of a dinner is caput cēnae (see main dish).
In Cicero a term of philosophy, more frequent from Pliny on. Via prīncipālis was the main street of a Roman camp (Liv. 10.33, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: of the first rank, leading, prime
evidence: Cic. Sen. 61: populī prīmārium fuisse virum
terms.comment: One of the first, chief in rank: a leading man or woman of the city (Cic.); of things, first-rate (Plaut.). Of persons more than of matters; for the main point see caput est above.

phrases.latin: cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum et īnservīre līberīs
phrases.english: whose chief praise was to look after the house and devote herself to the children

phrases.latin: et, id quod caput est, nōbīs inter nōs nostra sīve incommoda sīve vitia sīve injūriās esse tolerandās
phrases.english: and, what is the main thing, that we must bear with one another’s annoyances, faults and wrongs

principalis.html: From prīnceps, which de Vaan derives from prīmus and capiō (p. 489, s.v. prīmus). Traupman 343 marks it.
